entries.appliesTo: frontier developers of frontier models (foundation models trained with >10^26 operations); heightened duties on large frontier developers (annual gross revenues over $500,000,000)

dutySources.risk-program: § 10(a) — 'a large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework'
dutySources.documentation: § 10(c)(1) — 'Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version of an existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report'
dutySources.impact-assessment: § 10(e) — 'A large frontier developer shall transmit to the Agency a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use of its frontier models every 3 months'
dutySources.incident-reporting: § 15(c) — 'A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours'
dutySources.registration-filing: § 18(a) — 'no large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model, in whole or in part in this State, without having a current disclosure statement filed with the Agency and paying the required fee'
dutySources.takedown-process: § 20(e)(1) — 'A large frontier developer shall provide a reasonable internal process through which a covered employee may anonymously disclose information to the large frontier developer'

exposure.enforcer: attorney-general (exclusive civil action); Agency (IEMA) levies registration/disclosure penalties after notice and hearing

sources.threshold: § 5 — '"Frontier model" means a foundation model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10 26 integer or floating-point operations' (10^26; superscript split in extracted text)
sources.safetyFramework: § 10(a) — 'shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework'
sources.incidentReporting: § 15(c) — 'shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours'
sources.thirdPartyAudit: § 10(d) — 'a large frontier developer shall annually retain a third party to perform an independent audit of compliance with the requirements of this Section'
sources.whistleblower: § 20(a) — 'A frontier developer shall not make, adopt, enforce, or enter into a rule, regulation, policy, or contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing, or retaliates against a covered employee for disclosing, information'
sources.penaltyMax: § 25(a) — 'For a subsequent violation, the civil penalty may not exceed $3,000,000 per violation.'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 25(a) — 'a civil penalty in an amount dependent upon the severity of the violation that does not exceed $1,000,000 for the first violation. For a subsequent violation, the civil penalty may not exceed $3,000,000 per violation.'
sources.enforcer: § 25(b) — 'recovered in a civil action brought exclusively by the Attorney General'; § 18(e) — 'the Agency may, after notice and hearing, levy civil penalties, fees, and costs'

flags: Penalty tiers: first violation capped at $1,000,000, subsequent violations at $3,000,000 per violation (§ 25(a)); separate registration penalty of '$1,000 for each day the person fails to file a disclosure' plus assessments owed (§ 18(e)); penaltyMax codes the highest stated cap.

Dual thresholds: compute (>10^26 operations) defines 'frontier developer'; revenue ('annual gross revenues in excess of $500,000,000', § 5) defines 'large frontier developer', who bears most duties (framework, audit, registration, internal whistleblower process) — 'threshold: compute' alone is lossy.
Staggered effective dates: Act effective January 1, 2027 (§ 99); frontier AI framework and annual audit duties begin January 1, 2028 (§§ 10(a), 10(d)); registration begins January 1, 2027 (§ 18(a)).

§ 17 interoperability: a developer declaring intent to comply with a designated substantially-equivalent federal law, regulation, or guidance 'shall be deemed in compliance with this Act' to that extent.
§ 18(d) requires each large frontier developer to pay 'its pro rata share of the cost of administration of this Act' as an annual fee — no fixed fee amount stated.
Annual third-party audit (§ 10(d)) is a compliance audit, not a discrimination audit — captured in the thirdPartyAudit param; bias-audit duty not assigned.
takedown-process is coded for the § 20(e) internal anonymous disclosure channel, which is employee-facing (whistleblower), not a user-facing complaint/removal channel — lossy fit noted.
§ 10(f) prohibits materially false or misleading statements about catastrophic risk or framework compliance; no standalone duty key fits (conduct prohibition, coded via exposure only).
§§ 80 and 90 make conforming amendments to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA exemption for incident reports) and the Whistleblower Act (retaliation for disclosing violations of this Act).
No private right of action: § 25(d) — 'Nothing in this Act shall be construed to establish a private right of action'.
§ 35 home rule preemption: regulation of frontier models is 'an exclusive power and function of the State'.
